Every glb is in mm with z up, in the part's own frame; place it at `place` (three.js Euler XYZ, degrees) under its parent, the car's frame for a top-level part (D-418).
No place here is measured: every unit, the PMU, the left plate and every far end is a judgement inside its 00-CAR zone box, confirm until the dash is measured (C4, V-102, V-113).
The PMU stands for the dash node: every leg and drop meets it at the dash post (modules PMU: Dash node).
A link is a straight line from connector to connector, not the wire's run: the harness drawings (D-385) stay the wire's truth.
The boards show every part they draw, DNP ones too - the worst case the mock-ups' fit checks use.
The dash post is a cluster of receptacles beside the PMU, a row per leg (L1 at the top), 20 mm apart, each plug mated, facing the cabin - a judgement until the post is designed and measured.
The battery, disconnect, Class-T, MRBF holders and amplifier are moved to the passenger-side cargo bin (D-449); the devices builder had no node for it.

Devices stand where they are fitted (SPOTS in export_glb.py, judgement) and a housing named in such a device's devices.plug beside it; the rest stand on a shelf centred on their node, 5 mm apart (the devices 10), rows wrapping at 600 mm - the dash node's relays and fuses, the sill node's, the seats', the speakers'.
Housings no leg reaches (drawn at their node, on no leg's list): DP-DIAG.

Each leg is drawn as it will be built (D-583): a taped trunk from the dash post along the body - the firewall, the dash rail, the tunnel's sides, the sills, the inner wing, the hinge loop (TRUNKS in export_glb.py, judgement) - and from it a breakout to each housing and device, in straight runs along the car's axes and up the side wall where it climbs behind the dash, bent round 25 mm. A run's thickness is 1.2 x the root of the sum of its conductors' squared diameters (TXL-class, confirm), so the trunk thins as each breakout leaves it. The Audio runs (RT30-RT32) are a leg of their own from the head unit; a link is data (what mates what), not drawn.
